default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-298.title: Broadening-window micro-break fade
E-298.hypothesis: When the last block made both a higher high and a lower low than the block before it, the market is a megaphone: two-sided stop runs by players who push each edge to trigger the other side and then reverse; a further short-term break in that state is one more head-fake that the responsive side sells (buys), so fade it.

E-299.title: Weaker-than-the-level break fade
E-299.hypothesis: The bar that set the recent high was where the seller who capped it traded; a later close through that high on less volume than that bar means the breakers are smaller than the participant who defended the level, so his remaining size and the breakout buyers' stops reverse the break (mirror at the low).

E-300.title: Stale micro-level break follow
E-300.hypothesis: A window high made early in the window and not approached in the recent part of it has had time to collect the stops of shorts and the buy-stops of breakout traders; the first close through such a stale level releases that pile at once and the market orders carry the price on, unlike a level made a few bars ago.

E-301.title: Light-participation day micro-break fade
E-301.hypothesis: When the session's cumulative volume is well below its usual level for the time of day, the large institutional parent orders are absent and the book is run by local liquidity providers; short-term breaks then carry no initiator behind them and are leaned back, so fade them on light days.

E-302.title: Flattening-hour micro-break fade
E-302.hypothesis: In the last hour or two before the close, day traders who must be flat stop opening positions and only unwind, and position takers have done their day; short-term breaks then are bursts of liquidation into a book that refills, not new information, so fade them.

E-303.title: Day-after-trend-day micro-break fade
E-303.hypothesis: A session that closed at its high or low was a trend day (Raschke, Crabel); the next session usually digests it in a range while the trend-day holders take profit and late entrants rebalance, so its short-term breaks are faded.

E-304.title: High bar-overlap micro-break fade
E-304.hypothesis: When consecutive bars overlap far more than usual, every bar trades back through the previous one: the auction is rotating two-way with liquidity providers on both sides; a close beyond the window extreme in such a tape is one more rotation reaching an edge, so fade it.

E-305.title: Range-completion-schedule late extreme fade
E-305.hypothesis: The share of the day's final range already traded by each minute is stable across sessions; a new session high/low made at a time when, on recent days, the range was normally almost complete is an overshoot by late chasers that the day's done participants sell (buy) into, so fade it.

E-306.title: Long-detached-from-VWAP micro-break fade
E-306.hypothesis: After price has traded entirely on one side of the session VWAP for a long time, everyone who traded at value is in profit and benchmark desks are behind; a new short-term break further away is where those holders take profit and VWAP-benchmarked orders lean against it, so fade the break (not the VWAP cross of E-001).

E-307.title: Window volume-centre lag break fade
E-307.hypothesis: If the window's volume-weighted price sits below its plain average price, most contracts changed hands at the low side of the window: the up-moves came on little volume; an up-break of such a window is a light probe away from where the size traded and returns to it, so fade it (mirror for down-breaks).
